blocks.title: Acceptance testing
blocks.text: Acceptance testing is the final level of testing, carried out to decide whether the software is ready for release. It is often done by the end-users or clients to make sure the software meets their expectations and requirements.

It can be formal or informal and usually uses scenarios that copy real-world use to check the software's usability, reliability and performance. Because end-users often do it, acceptance testing is sometimes called User Acceptance Testing (UAT) (Did You Know).
